record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Is every computably enumerable degree, or at least some computably enumerable degree, realized as the degree of topological categoricity of a computable Polish space?

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Is every/any c.e. degree the degree of topological categoricity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A Polish space is a topological space homeomorphic to a complete separable metric space. A computable Polish space is given by a computable presentation: a countable dense sequence (xi)_{i∈ω} together with a complete computable metric d, i.e. d(xi,xj) is uniformly computable as a real. A homeomorphism between two computable Polish spaces is called d-computable, for a Turing degree d, if its graph (equivalently, the map between the dense sequences viewed as points of the spaces) can be effectively computed using a d-oracle in the standard sense of computable analysis.

For a computable Polish space X, define its degree of topological categoricity (when it exists) to be the least Turing degree d such that for every pair of computable presentations of X (as a Polish space, i.e. up to homeomorphism), there is a d-computable homeomorphism between them, and such that d is the minimum among all degrees with this property.

Question. Determine whether the following holds:
(a) every computably enumerable Turing degree is the degree of topological categoricity of some computable Polish space; or, failing that,
(b) at least one (nonzero) computably enumerable Turing degree is realized as the degree of topological categoricity of some computable Polish space.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on computable Polish spaces and effective categoricity (e.g., work on computable Stone spaces, effectively categorical compact Polish spaces, and computable categoricity relative to a c.e. degree) discusses related questions but does not record a resolution of the specific question asking which c.e. degrees are realized as degrees of topological categoricity of computable Polish spaces. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Computable categoricity relative to a c.e. degree
status_evidence.snippet: Studies computable categoricity of structures relative to a c.e. degree, but in the algebraic-structures setting.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work on c.e. degrees and categoricity, not resolving the topological-Polish-space version.

status_evidence.title: Computable Stone Spaces (arXiv:2107.01536)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops effective categoricity for classes of computable Polish-type spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides framework for topological categoricity but does not classify c.e. categoricity degrees of computable Polish spaces.
